notes: JAMB Government 2026 — 100 questions (mock/predicted + style-matched items). Not official JAMB papers.

questions.prompt: The system of government in Nigeria since 1999 is?
questions.explanation: Nigeria operates a presidential system with separation of powers between the executive, legislature, and judiciary since the return to civil rule in 1999.

questions.prompt: Socialism developed as a protest against the evils of?
questions.explanation: Socialism emerged in the 19th century as a reaction to the exploitation, inequality, and poor working conditions caused by capitalism during the Industrial Revolution.

questions.prompt: Who among the following is associated with fascism?
questions.explanation: Benito Mussolini founded the Fascist Party in Italy and ruled as a fascist dictator. Stalin is associated with Communism, while Marx and Engels are the fathers of Socialism/Communism.

questions.prompt: Fascism as a system of government originated in?
questions.explanation: Fascism first emerged as a ruling system in Italy in 1922 under Benito Mussolini, before spreading to Germany as Nazism.

questions.prompt: Government of the few over the majority is?
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is derived from the Greek words oligos (few) and arkhein (rule), literally defining a system where power resides in the hands of a small number of people.

questions.prompt: The central point of capitalism as expounded by Karl Marx is that?
options: Capitalists’ profit is the surplus value obtained from workers’ labour
Workers are inherently incapable of being owners of their labour
Capitalists shall always increase workers’ earning capacity through wages
Capitalists shall always readily share profits with workers
questions.explanation: Marx’s “Theory of Surplus Value” argues that capitalists exploit workers by paying them less than the value of what they produce.

questions.prompt: A fundamental principle of a democratic government is?
questions.explanation: Democracy requires active participation from citizens in decision-making through voting, freedom of expression, and civic engagement. Options A, B, and D are anti-democratic.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a source of public opinion?
questions.explanation: Public opinion is shaped by sources that reflect the views of the masses. Academic journals are typically restricted to scholarly research and do not represent the general public’s sentiment.

questions.prompt: The principle of collective responsibility is central to?
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, cabinet ministers are jointly responsible to parliament for government decisions.

questions.prompt: Power differs from influence in that it is?
questions.explanation: Power involves the ability to compel obedience, often through coercion or sanctions, while influence relies on persuasion.

questions.prompt: Separation of powers was propounded by?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu articulated the doctrine of separation of powers in The Spirit of Laws (1748).

questions.prompt: A body established and entrusted with power and authority to direct the affairs of the state is called?
questions.explanation: Government is the institution established to direct and manage the affairs of the state.

questions.prompt: The institutions which constitute the main organs of the government of a nation are the?
questions.explanation: The three main organs of government are the legislature (lawmaking), executive (implementation), and judiciary (interpretation).

questions.prompt: The type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is?
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty rests on the consent and legitimacy of the governed.

questions.prompt: A major advantage of the principle of separation of powers is that it provides for?
questions.explanation: Separation of powers creates a system of checks and balances among the three arms of government.

questions.prompt: The 1979 and 1999 Constitutions are similar because both?
options: Require 2/3 majority of the National Assembly + 2/3 of state assemblies for amendment
Abolish the office of the president
questions.explanation: Both constitutions have rigid amendment procedures requiring a two-thirds majority of the National Assembly and two-thirds of state assemblies.

questions.prompt: Items on the Exclusive Legislative List can only be legislated by?
questions.explanation: The Exclusive Legislative List (Second Schedule, Part I) contains matters reserved exclusively for the federal legislature, such as defence, currency, and foreign affairs.

questions.prompt: Nigeria became a republic in?
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963, when Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first President.

questions.prompt: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced?
options: The first election of Nigerians into the Legislative Council
The office of the Prime Minister
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution introduced the first elective principle, allowing four Nigerians to be elected into the Legislative Council.

questions.prompt: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 established?
options: True federal structure with regional autonomy
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution established a true federal structure, granting substantial autonomy to the regions.

questions.prompt: The Richards Constitution of 1946 introduced?
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into three regions (North, West, and East), introducing the regional system.

questions.prompt: A constitution that requires special procedures for amendment is said to be?
questions.explanation: Rigid constitutions have cumbersome amendment procedures, often requiring supermajorities or referendums.

questions.prompt: The exclusive legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Exclusive list items are reserved for the federal legislature alone.

questions.prompt: The concurrent legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Concurrent list items allow both federal and state legislatures to make laws, with federal law prevailing in case of conflict.

questions.prompt: The residuary legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Residuary matters are those not explicitly assigned to either level; they are often left to state governments in a federal system.

questions.prompt: An unwritten constitution is found in?
questions.explanation: The UK has an uncodified constitution derived from statutes, conventions, and judicial decisions.

questions.prompt: Constitutionalism implies?
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism is the principle that governmental power should be legally limited and constrained by a constitution.

questions.prompt: Judicial review is the power of the courts to?
questions.explanation: Judicial review empowers courts to review and invalidate legislative or executive actions that violate the constitution.

questions.prompt: A constitution that can be amended by ordinary legislative process is?
questions.explanation: Flexible constitutions can be amended through the same procedure as ordinary laws.

questions.prompt: The fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy were first introduced in Nigeria by the?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced these principles as a guide for public policy and governance.

questions.prompt: The head of the Nigerian judiciary is the?
options: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: Section 230(1) of the 1999 Constitution establishes the Chief Justice of Nigeria as the head of the judiciary.

questions.prompt: The Public Complaints Commission is also called?
questions.explanation: The Public Complaints Commission is Nigeria’s ombudsman, established to investigate administrative injustice.

questions.prompt: The Nigerian Police Force is under the?
options: Federal government (supervised by the Minister of Interior)
questions.explanation: Section 215 of the 1999 Constitution places the Nigeria Police Force under federal control, supervised by the Minister of Interior.

questions.prompt: The primary function of the legislature is to?
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws.

questions.prompt: The executive arm of government is responsible for?
questions.explanation: The executive implements laws and administers public affairs.

questions.prompt: The judiciary is independent when?
options: It is funded by the executive
It is free from external influence in its decisions
It takes directives from the legislature
questions.explanation: Judicial independence requires that courts decide cases impartially, free from political or other improper influence.

questions.prompt: A civil service is described as anonymous because?
options: Civil servants are unknown to the public
Individual civil servants are not personally credited or blamed for official actions
questions.explanation: Anonymity means civil servants work behind the scenes, with actions attributed to the government or department rather than individuals.

questions.prompt: The permanent secretary in a ministry is?
options: The administrative head of the ministry
questions.explanation: The permanent secretary is the senior civil servant who heads the administrative machinery of a ministry.

questions.prompt: The principle of collective responsibility applies to?
options: The cabinet in a parliamentary system
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary cabinet, ministers are collectively responsible for government decisions and must publicly support them or resign.

questions.prompt: A bill is a?
questions.explanation: A bill is a draft legislative proposal that becomes law only after passage through the legislature and assent.

questions.prompt: The process of manipulating constituency boundaries to favour a particular party is called?
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of electoral boundaries for partisan advantage.

questions.prompt: The Code of Conduct Bureau is established to?
options: Protect public officers from the press
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau enforces ethical standards and asset declaration rules for public officers to promote accountability.

questions.prompt: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has the power to prepare and maintain the register of?
questions.explanation: INEC is responsible for compiling and updating the voter register for elections.

questions.prompt: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is headed by the?
options: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of Nigeria is the highest judicial officer and heads the Supreme Court.

questions.prompt: The Court of Appeal is headed by the?
options: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: The President of the Court of Appeal heads that court and is second in judicial hierarchy.

questions.prompt: The process of removing a judge for misconduct is called?
questions.explanation: Impeachment is the formal constitutional process for removing senior public officials, including judges, for misconduct.

questions.prompt: The Attorney-General of the Federation is the?
options: Chief law officer of the federal government
Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The Attorney-General is the chief legal adviser and prosecutor for the federal government.

questions.prompt: Delegated legislation is criticized because it?
options: Undermines the principle of separation of powers
questions.explanation: Delegated legislation transfers lawmaking power to the executive, which critics argue undermines the separation of powers and democratic accountability.

questions.prompt: The standing committee of a legislature is one that?
options: Is permanently established to handle specific policy areas
questions.explanation: Standing committees are permanent legislative committees that handle specific policy areas and continue from session to session.

questions.prompt: The concept of checks and balances empowers the judiciary to?
questions.explanation: Judicial review allows courts to check the other branches by declaring actions that violate the constitution null and void.

questions.prompt: Nigeria became a republic in?
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963, when Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first President.

questions.prompt: The first political party in Nigeria was the?
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
questions.explanation: The NNDP, founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923, was Nigeria’s first political party.

questions.prompt: A major issue that distinguishes pressure groups from political parties is that pressure groups?
options: Seek to influence policy rather than capture power
questions.explanation: Pressure groups aim to influence government decisions without seeking to govern directly, whereas political parties contest elections to form government.

questions.prompt: The major advantage of the secret ballot is that it?
options: Ensures free and fair elections by protecting voter privacy
questions.explanation: The secret ballot protects voters from intimidation and victimization, ensuring their choices remain private.

questions.prompt: The Igbo political system was based on?
questions.explanation: The pre-colonial Igbo political system was largely decentralized and republican, with authority vested in councils of elders and age grades rather than a single ruler.

questions.prompt: A major defect of the 1979 Constitution was that?
options: It abolished the office of the president
It created a weak federal government
It was promulgated by a military decree without a referendum
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution was handed down by the military (Decree No. 12 of 1979) without a popular referendum, a major criticism of its legitimacy.

questions.prompt: In a federal system, residual powers are vested in the?
questions.explanation: Residual powers—matters not explicitly assigned to the federal government—are left to the states in a federal system.

questions.prompt: The federal character principle in Nigeria is intended to?
options: Ensure equitable representation of diverse groups in national institutions
questions.explanation: Federal character aims to reflect Nigeria’s ethnic and regional diversity in appointments and distribution of resources.

questions.prompt: The concept of political socialization refers to?
options: The process by which individuals acquire political beliefs and values
questions.explanation: Political socialization is the lifelong process through which individuals develop their political attitudes, beliefs, and behaviours.

questions.prompt: The Nigerian civil war was caused by?
options: The massacres of Igbo people and the secession of Biafra
questions.explanation: The 1966 massacres of Igbo people in the North and the subsequent declaration of Biafra were major triggers of the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.prompt: Nigeria’s federal system is characterized by?
options: Division of powers between federal and state governments
questions.explanation: Federalism in Nigeria divides authority between the federal government and state governments, with local governments as a third tier.

questions.prompt: The 1963 Republican Constitution made Nigeria a?
questions.explanation: The 1963 Constitution abolished the Queen as head of state and established a Nigerian president as ceremonial head of state.

questions.prompt: Who reorganised Nigeria’s four regions into twelve states in May 1967?
questions.explanation: General Gowon created 12 states in 1967 to reduce regional tensions and strengthen central authority.

questions.prompt: Under the 1999 Constitution, the power to create local governments is vested in the?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution empowers State Houses of Assembly to create and abolish local government areas.

questions.prompt: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about?
questions.explanation: Without the rule of law, arbitrary exercise of power can lead to rights violations and abuse.

questions.prompt: The electoral system that requires a candidate to obtain more than 50% of valid votes cast to be declared winner is?
questions.explanation: The absolute majority system requires a candidate to secure more than half (50% + 1) of the valid votes cast to win outright.

questions.prompt: In the Nigerian presidential election system, a candidate must obtain the highest number of votes and at least?
options: One-quarter of votes in two-thirds of all states
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution requires a presidential candidate to have the highest number of votes and at least one-quarter of the votes in each of at least two-thirds of all the states and the FCT.

questions.prompt: The electoral system where seats are allocated to political parties based on the percentage of votes they receive is called?
questions.explanation: Proportional representation allocates legislative seats in proportion to the share of votes each party receives.

questions.prompt: A major disadvantage of the proportional representation system is that it?
options: Often leads to coalition governments and political instability
questions.explanation: Because no single party may win a majority under PR, coalition governments are common, which can lead to instability.

questions.prompt: The practice of dividing an electoral constituency to give unfair advantage to a particular party is called?
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries to favour a particular party or candidate.

questions.prompt: Which electoral body is responsible for conducting federal elections in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: INEC is the constitutionally mandated body to organize federal elections in Nigeria.

questions.prompt: An election conducted to choose a party flagbearer is a?
questions.explanation: A primary election is an internal party election to select a candidate for a general election.

questions.prompt: A by-election is held to?
options: Fill a vacant seat between general elections
questions.explanation: By-elections are held to fill casual vacancies arising between general elections.

questions.prompt: A referendum is a process in which?
options: Citizens vote directly on a specific issue or policy
questions.explanation: A referendum allows the electorate to approve or reject a specific proposal directly.

questions.prompt: An electoral malpractice includes?
questions.explanation: Ballot stuffing is a form of electoral fraud where illegitimate votes are added to the count.

questions.prompt: A pressure group that seeks to promote the interests of workers is a?
questions.explanation: Trade unions are pressure groups that represent and protect the interests of workers.

questions.prompt: The Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) is an example of a?
questions.explanation: The NLC is a federation of trade unions that acts as a pressure group on labour and economic issues.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a pressure group?
questions.explanation: The NBA is a professional association that advocates for legal professionals and justice-related issues.

questions.prompt: A political party that is dominant in a political system is called a?
questions.explanation: The ruling party is the party that holds governmental power after winning elections.

questions.prompt: The opposition party in a democracy is important because it?
options: Checks the excesses of the ruling party
questions.explanation: Opposition parties provide alternative policies and hold the government accountable.

questions.prompt: A coalition government is formed when?
options: One party wins an outright majority
Two or more parties combine to form a government
questions.explanation: Coalition governments arise when no single party has a majority, prompting parties to cooperate.

questions.prompt: The first political party in Nigeria was the?
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
questions.explanation: The NNDP, founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923, was Nigeria’s first political party.

questions.prompt: In the First Republic, the official opposition party was the?
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: The Action Group, led by Obafemi Awolowo, served as the official opposition in the First Republic.

questions.prompt: The right to vote is known as?
questions.explanation: The franchise (or suffrage) is the legal right to vote in political elections.

questions.prompt: A major feature of the policy of deregulation in Nigeria is the?
options: Reduction of government involvement in economic activities
questions.explanation: Deregulation reduces government interference and control in key sectors, allowing market forces to operate more freely.

questions.prompt: Nigeria is NOT a member of?
questions.explanation: NATO is a Western military alliance; Nigeria is not a member.

questions.prompt: The charter of the United Nations was drawn up in?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

questions.prompt: ECOWAS was established in?
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was founded in 1975 through the Treaty of Lagos.

questions.prompt: The headquarters of ECOWAS is located in?
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission is headquartered in Abuja, Nigeria.

questions.prompt: The main problem of ECOWAS is lack of?
questions.explanation: A recurring challenge for ECOWAS has been inadequate political will among member states to implement collective decisions.

questions.prompt: Nigeria became a member of OPEC in?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries in 1971.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a founding member of OPEC?
questions.explanation: Venezuela was one of the five founding members of OPEC in 1960.

questions.prompt: The African Union (AU) was established in?
questions.explanation: The AU was formally launched in 2002, succeeding the Organization of African Unity (OAU).

questions.prompt: The headquarters of the African Union is in?
questions.explanation: The AU headquarters is located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.prompt: The United Nations Security Council has how many permanent members?
questions.explanation: The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

questions.prompt: The ECOWAS Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was organized to maintain peace in?
questions.explanation: ECOMOG was deployed to Liberia in 1990 and later to Sierra Leone to restore peace during civil conflicts.

questions.prompt: Nigeria’s non-aligned policy means that she will?
options: Have nothing to do with the superpowers
Not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations
Avoid having any dealing with any country with ideological leanings
Relate only with member countries of the Non-Aligned Movement
questions.explanation: Non-alignment means Nigeria avoids committing to either Cold War bloc and makes decisions based on national interests.

questions.prompt: The Commonwealth is an association of?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of mostly former territories of the British Empire.

questions.prompt: Nigeria became a member of the United Nations in?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the UN on 7 October 1960, shortly after gaining independence.

questions.prompt: The principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of other states is a cornerstone of?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter enshrines the principle of non-interference in the domestic jurisdiction of sovereign states.
